chapters.title: Why you're still in it
chapters.teaser: The real reason your soul keeps saying 'let's see where it goes'.

chapters.title: What you actually want
chapters.teaser: Not what sounds chill. What you'd ask for if you weren't worried.

chapters.title: How you read mixed signals
chapters.teaser: Your decoding habit, and a better way to get information.

chapters.title: The talk, your way
chapters.teaser: How to ask 'what are we' in words that fit your soul.

chapters.title: Your line
chapters.teaser: The one thing you shouldn't keep accepting.

chapters.title: Either way, you're okay
chapters.teaser: What comes next, whatever answer you get.

text.why-you-stay: Gyeong Metal is the blade, direct and loyal. Honestly, situationships aren't your natural habitat, because you like things clear and labeled. So if you're in one, something about this person got past your defences. You might be staying out of pride, not wanting to be the one who cares more first. Or you said casual at the beginning, and you keep your word even when it no longer fits. Check whether that early promise still matches who you are now, or whether you're just being loyal to an old sentence.
text.what-you-want: You want clarity and loyalty, plainly. Gyeong Metal knows this about itself. You might have avoided saying it because asking feels like showing weakness, like handing over a point. It isn't. A direct question is your superpower, and you use it brilliantly everywhere else in your life. You want to know where you stand, and you want to stand somewhere solid. That's a completely fair want. Not asking doesn't make you cooler. It just keeps you in a gray zone you actively dislike. Say it the way you'd say anything else important to you: simply, calmly, and once, without decoration.
text.mixed-signals: Mixed signals frustrate you more than most people. Gyeong Metal sees in black and white, and gray can feel almost like disrespect. You might respond by going cold, quietly testing them, or delivering an ultimatum far too early. Try something in between those options: a calm, direct question. Not a test. Not a verdict. Just: where are we? You'll learn more from one honest question than from three weeks of silent observation, and you'll keep your dignity fully intact. If you notice yourself drafting an ultimatum in your head, take that as a cue to ask the question instead.
text.the-talk: You'll handle the talk well, as long as it stays a conversation and not a cross-examination. Gyeong Metal can sound sharper than intended, especially when nervous. Soften the delivery, not the content. I like you. I want something clear. What do you want? Then let them think for a moment. A slow answer isn't automatically a bad answer, and people who are put on the spot often say less than they mean. Give the silence a little room before you draw any conclusions. Keep your arms uncrossed and your tone level. Your words are already clear, so let your body language be easy.
text.your-line: Your non-negotiable is honesty. Gyeong Metal can handle hard truths, but not being kept vague or misled. Decide clearly what you won't accept: dodging the question again and again, hidden other people, promises that never match actions. When it's crossed, you step away cleanly. You don't need a speech or a final word. You don't need to prove they were wrong. Just leave with your head up. Walking away calmly says everything a speech would say, with better posture. Decide your line on a calm day, before you're angry, so it reflects your values rather than your mood.
text.either-way: Whichever way it goes, you come out clear, which is what you wanted all along. If they want more, you'll build it with your usual fierce loyalty. If not, you'll cut cleanly and probably feel it later, quietly, when you least expect it. Let yourself feel it when it arrives. Strength and sadness can share a room without either one winning. Then go back to the people who already know exactly where they stand with you, because you told them. Go to the gym, call your oldest friend, and let both of those count as taking care of yourself.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You care about honesty more than anything, Gyeong.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Then why are you in a situationship? That's your opposite.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Asking where you stand isn't weakness.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Ask once. Calmly. No interrogation lamp.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Soften the delivery, keep the message.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: If they dodge the question twice, that's the answer.

spring.intro: A spring axe faces a whole forest, and Your birth season belonged to Wood, Gyeong. Metal cuts Wood, so you're wired to act, decide and conquer what's in front of you. In a situationship the ambiguity is almost physically uncomfortable. You might have asked about it already, bluntly, and been told it's complicated. Or you might be treating them like a project to win. Spring Gyeong's blind spot is chasing: too many trees, all hacked at once. Instead of pushing for an answer, state your position once, clearly, and stop. Your directness is a gift when you say it and then let them choose.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: State it once, Gyeong. Then stop swinging. Chasing isn't the same as clarity.

summer.intro: Summer-born metal was made in the forge. Fire was in command when you were born, Gyeong, and Fire melts Metal, so you're used to pressure and good at enduring heat. In a situationship you may be enduring too well. You tell yourself it's fine, you're tough, you don't need labels. Meanwhile the vagueness is quietly melting your patience. Summer Gyeong's risk is the sudden snap: weeks of silence, then one cold message that ends it. Before you get there, let the heat out in a measured way. Tell them what you want while you're still calm. A sword is strongest tempered, not overheated.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Say it while you're calm, Gyeong. Not after the snap.

autumn.intro: Autumn Gyeong is metal at its most absolute. Metal was in command when you were born and doubled your element, so you value loyalty, straight answers and clear lines. A situationship is the opposite of everything you trust. So why are you in one? Maybe because you're testing them silently, waiting to see if they're worthy before you commit. Strong Gyeong can hold out for the other person to prove themselves first, while they wait for the same from you. Two swords crossed, nobody moving. Lower yours slightly. Show your loyalty first. Then their response is the honest answer you've been waiting for.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Two people waiting to see who blinks first. Romance of the century, Gyeong.

winter.intro: Winter Gyeong is steel near a cold river. You were born while Water was in charge and Metal generates Water, so your strength flows out as thinking. In a situationship you probably analyze everything privately: what they meant, what they want, how it might go. You keep your face neutral and your feelings locked. They may genuinely not know you care. Winter Gyeong's blind spot is assuming your loyalty is obvious when you've never actually said it. Let the water carry a message. Say I like you, plainly. You're braver than almost anyone. Spend some of that courage on the soft words.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: They might not know you care, Gyeong. Tell them in plain words.

earth.intro: The Earth days feed Metal, and you were born in them, Gyeong: ore with plenty of mountain behind it. You feel secure in yourself, which makes you seem unbothered in a situationship. You won't chase. You also won't soften, so the other person may not know you care. The drift is mutual pride: neither of you wants to be the one who asks. The talk for you should be plain and short, which suits you. Here's what I want. What do you want? No debate, no scoring.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Not chasing is fine, Gyeong. Not saying anything at all is just stubborn.

strength.strong: Your chart reinforces your metal, Gyeong, so you're direct and quick to decide. In a situationship you might have issued an ultimatum already, or be close to it. Clarity is good. Ultimatums delivered like verdicts can make people defensive instead of honest. The blind spot of strong metal is cutting before the other person has had time to answer. Say what you want, then give them room. If you're tempted to end it in one sharp message, sleep on it first. Your edge works better tempered.
strength.weak: With little support for your Day Master, Gyeong, you act tough while bending more than you'd like. In a situationship you might say it's fine, act unbothered and then silently tolerate far less than you deserve. The blind spot is proving strength by needing nothing. Real strength says this is what I want, out loud. Practice it on something small: a plan you'd like, a day you'd prefer. Your no and your yes both deserve to be heard by the person you're seeing.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood means you push for growth and definition. In a situationship you might rush clarity, or picture a whole future before the other person has caught up to the present. Your drive is a good thing. Just give them room to answer at their own pace once you've asked. Ask once, clearly, then step back and let the answer come. Balance with a little Metal: clear boundaries, finished business, knowing when something needs pruning rather than more growth.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means starting things, including the talk, feels hard. You might let an undefined situation drift on and on simply because initiating anything feels heavy. Build momentum in small steps: decide what you want, write it down, choose a day to ask. Spend time outdoors and around green things. You don't need to grow everything at once. You only need one honest question, asked once, out loud.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire means big feelings, fast. In a situationship you might swing between excitement and frustration in the same evening, and want answers right now. Slow your pace a little. Pick a calm moment for the talk, not a heated one. Cool down with water: rest, quiet nights in, a walk before sending any big message. Your passion is attractive. Just don't let it make your decisions at midnight.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means expressing feelings and being seen can feel hard. You might keep this situationship low-key so that nobody, including you, has to admit it matters. Turn the light up a little. Let your feelings show in small ways. Be visible in your own life too: plans, friends, sunlight, music. The more you shine for yourself, the easier the honest question becomes when you finally ask it.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth means you wait, stay steady, and stay put, sometimes for too long. In a situationship you may tolerate a lack of definition because change feels disruptive and messy. Bring in a bit of movement: pick a day by which you'll have the talk, and keep it. Let some Wood in, growth and fresh starts. Stable doesn't have to mean stuck, and patient doesn't have to mean silent.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means stability is hard to find, and an undefined relationship can make you feel even more unsteady than usual. Ground yourself first: routines, regular meals, a dependable circle of friends. Then have the talk from a steady place, not a shaky one. You'll think more clearly and ask more clearly when your own ground is solid under your feet, whatever the answer turns out to be.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal means you want clarity and might cut too fast to get it. In a situationship you may issue ultimatums or go cold the moment things feel vague. Your boundaries are strong, which is good. Soften the delivery: ask with curiosity first, decide second. Water helps here: rest, reflection, letting a feeling be felt before you act on it.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are hard. In a situationship you may accept less than you want and keep telling yourself it's fine. Practice clear edges: decide your line and write it down somewhere you'll see it. Say no to plans that don't work for you. White and silver, decluttering, finishing things all support you. A boundary isn't harsh. It's honesty about what you need.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water means overthinking and very deep feeling. In a situationship you might analyze every message and drown in what-ifs that never happen. Your intuition is valuable, but it needs a shore to land on. Earth helps: routines, physical activity, friends who ground you. Put a limit on the analysis. Ask the question instead of guessing the answer.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means reflection and rest get skipped. You might keep the situationship busy and fun so you never have to stop and think about what it actually is. Make space for quiet: a journal, a slow evening, a moment alone to ask yourself what you really want here. Clarity starts inside you before it's ever spoken to them, and it's worth the quiet.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: you've planned your future together. They haven't planned Saturday.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: That growing energy is lovely. Point it at what you want, not only at them.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: one great date and you're naming the dog. Breathe.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is magnetic. Let them match it before you double it.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth: you've waited so patiently you've basically become their furniture.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness is a gift. It's fair to ask for steadiness back.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal: you've drafted an ultimatum. Maybe try a question first.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your clarity is strength. Soften the delivery and it lands beautifully.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you analyzed one 'haha' with three friends and a tarot app.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your sensitivity notices so much. Check the signals against actual actions too.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood can make it hard to picture what you want. Try imagining it.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: No Wood, no vision. You're seeing where it goes without looking anywhere.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can make it hard to show interest. A little warmth helps.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: No Fire. They genuinely cannot tell if you like them. Neither can I.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth makes it easy to drift. Choose one thing you're sure about.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth, no ground. You change your mind about them every other day.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal can blur your line. You can decide what you won't accept.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal means no line. You'll accept 'wyd' at midnight forever.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can make feelings hard to say. Try writing them first.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: No Water. You'd rather move countries than say 'I like you.'

gap-wood.title: Radio chatter and a dishwasher war
gap-wood.text: You like a Gap Wood because they stand for something. They have opinions, they hold their ground, they don't fold when you push. For you, that's rare and attractive. It's also the problem. You push to sharpen things; Gap hears an attack on their values and plants their feet. You only meant that the restaurant they chose was overpriced. Now you're debating ethics on the walk home. The drift in this pair is the constant low-level sparring. It's fun and it takes up all the space where tenderness would go. Neither of you has said 'I like you' in plain words, because it feels like conceding a round. Your texts are clipped, 'ok', 'fine', 'why', and Gap sends the same back, so nobody really knows where they stand. Your signal is challenge, which can read as disapproval. For the talk, put the blade down first. Gap needs to feel respected before anything else lands, so start there: I respect you a lot. I'd like us to be together properly. What do you want? Don't critique the answer. You can correct the dishwasher later. This one sentence matters more than being right.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You two agree on almost everything. Except who is right.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong, the dishwasher is not a referendum. Put the axe down.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gap owes one true sentence, not a sermon.

eul-wood.title: The blade asks, the vine sends a frog
eul-wood.text: With an Eul Wood, you get the classic 乙庚 pull: you're the blade, they're the vine, and somehow it works. Eul softens you. They make you laugh at yourself, which almost nobody manages. You text 'where are you.' and get a sticker of a frog, a voice note about a cat, and eventually an address. It drives you up the wall and you like it anyway. The drift starts when you push for an answer. Eul doesn't do direct confrontation. When you ask 'so what are we doing here', Eul tends to smile, say something charming, and leave you with nothing to hold. Then you get sharper, and sharpness cuts a vine more deeply than you realize. Eul's response to a cut is to slip sideways, and the loop speeds up. You might also catch yourself trying to toughen Eul up, which is not your job. For the talk, the fix is almost boring. Wait ten minutes before replying when annoyed. Then ask warmly, in person: I'm serious about you. I want this to be a real relationship. Do you? If the first answer wanders, ask again gently, without the edge. Steel can be clear without being cold.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: 乙庚 is a real pull. Steel and vine, oddly perfect.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Eul should answer 'where are you' with an address. Then the frog.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gyeong, wait ten minutes. Then be warm and clear.

byeong-fire.title: Caps lock versus 'ok.'
byeong-fire.text: A Byeong Fire is loud, warm and impossible to ignore. They walk into your structured week and set it on fire, in a good way, mostly. You find it attractive that they're so alive, and slightly exhausting that they need you to react to all of it. The drift here is temperature. Byeong sends a message with seven emojis about something exciting. You reply 'ok' or 'nice'. To you, that's fine. To Byeong, that's a bucket of cold water. Byeong wants warmth and celebration; you want respect and results, and you show care by doing things, not saying things. When Byeong pushes for more, you resist being melted, and when you're blunt, Byeong's light dims. Arguments get loud, and you both want the last word. The question of what this is gets drowned out by who was right. Your signal is restraint, which a sun can read as disapproval. For the talk, decide it face to face, never by text. Start with something genuinely warm, said out loud: I like you more than I've shown. I'd like us to be a proper couple. Do you? And add a word of praise now and then. It costs you a second.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Byeong missed it: Gyeong's 'nice' was high praise. Truly.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Never fight by text. Caps lock versus 'ok.' is a disaster.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gyeong, one warm word out loud. It costs a second.

jeong-fire.title: Forgotten by dinner, replayed at midnight
jeong-fire.text: A Jeong Fire is warm, careful and quietly intense. You like that they don't make noise. You like that they think before they speak. You also notice that they seem to go quiet at strange moments, and you're not always sure why. Here's a likely reason: you said something blunt. Not cruel, just direct. You moved on by dinner. Jeong may still be turning it over at midnight. That gap in memory causes more trouble in this pair than any actual issue. Jeong communicates in code when hurt, a shorter reply, a cooler tone, and you don't speak code. You want it said. Jeong wants it noticed. The situationship can sit in that standoff for a long time, with you assuming things are fine because no one complained. Your signal is decisiveness, which can feel harsh to a candle. For the talk, soften the tone and keep the clarity: I care about you, more than I probably show. I'd like us to be together. How do you feel about that? Then ask, kindly, if anything you've said has stung. There may be a short list. Listen to it without defending.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Patient heat, slow shaping. This can be something.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong forgot the fight by dinner. Jeong is still drafting a reply.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Say it the same day. No midnight replays.

mu-earth.title: Decide tonight or sleep on it for a week
mu-earth.text: A Mu Earth holds you the way a mountain holds ore. They're solid, loyal and unflustered. You never have to guess where you stand with a Mu on most things. Except, apparently, this one. The drift here is speed. You like to decide things. You'd have the 'what are we' talk tonight, settle it, and move on. Mu needs time to think, and when you push, Mu goes still. You read that stillness as dodging and get blunter, and Mu, who doesn't show hurt easily, quietly digs in. Two proud people, short texts on both sides, no apologies. The situationship can freeze into a standoff where neither of you mentions it again. Your signal is urgency, which a mountain can feel as pressure to move before it's ready. For the talk, make the question clear and let Mu set the pace of the answer: I'd like us to be official. Think about it, and tell me when you're ready. Then actually wait. Patience is not your talent, but it's the respect a Mu responds to. Meanwhile, add one personal line to your messages. Not because you need to. Because Mu notices.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Strength protecting strength. You two make a solid team.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong wants an answer tonight. Mu wants a week. Meet at Sunday.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Slow is not the same as unsure.

gi-earth.title: 'Done. Coming home.' and the question nobody answered
gi-earth.text: A Gi Earth makes your life better in ways you don't always see. The meal ready when you come home. The reminder about your brother's birthday. The calm voice when work was a war. You feel steady around Gi, and you might not have told them that. The drift here is that you lean on Gi's support and forget to check if Gi is okay. You text 'done. coming home.' Gi asks how it went, and you don't really answer. You make decisions quickly and Gi tends to go along, holding back quieter opinions to avoid your impatience. When you're blunt, Gi takes it inside. Over time, Gi can start to feel less like a partner and more like staff, and from where you stand, everything looks fine. Your signal is decisiveness, which can steamroll someone who doesn't push back. For the talk, start with gratitude, specific and out loud. Then ask, don't announce: I'd like us to be together properly. What do you want? And what would help you feel looked after? Then answer the question Gi asks you, fully. And send something just because, not because you need something.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Fertile ground for raw ore. Patience that shapes strength.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong, Gi asked how your day went. Answer it.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi is a partner, not support staff. Saying so matters.

gyeong-metal.title: 'Where.' 'Here.' 'Ok.'
gyeong-metal.text: Two Gyeong Metals in a situationship are loyal, honest and armed. Your texts are a comedy of efficiency: 'Where.' 'Here.' 'Ok.' Nobody wastes a word. You respect each other immediately, and you'd both defend the other in a bar argument without being asked. You have not, however, said a single soft thing out loud. The drift for two blades is pride. Neither of you softens your words, and both of you believe you're just being honest. A small disagreement about directions can turn into a battle of will on the pavement. Vulnerability feels like weakness to both of you, so hurt comes out as irritation, and the 'what are we' question sits there because asking it would mean admitting you want something. Someone is also keeping a tally of who apologized last. You both know it. For the talk, one of you has to lower the blade first, and it doesn't count as losing: I like you. I want this to be serious. Your turn. Say it plainly, then add an emoji to the next text. Not because either of you needs it. Because it's funny, and funny is how two Gyeongs say tender.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Two blades crossed. Loyal to the bone, the pair of you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: 'Where.' 'Here.' 'Ok.' Romantic. Truly.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Lower the blade first. It doesn't count as losing.

sin-metal.title: One true sentence, one perfectly cold reply
sin-metal.text: A Sin Metal is steel's polished cousin. Same element, completely different finish. You find Sin elegant, clever and slightly intimidating in a way you won't admit. Sin finds you strong and direct, and also occasionally like someone who walked into a jewelry shop wearing boots. The drift in this situationship has a classic opening. You say something true in the worst possible way. Sin answers with one perfectly cold sentence. Then you're both too proud to talk for a day. You think Sin is nitpicking. Sin thinks you're careless with their polish. Neither apologizes first, and the question of what you are gets stuck behind whichever silence is current. Sin also communicates in subtext, and you miss subtext entirely. A slightly delayed reply, a story post with a sharp caption, all of that goes past you. Your signal is directness, which Sin can feel as a scratch. For the talk, soften the delivery and keep the honesty. Pick a moment when neither of you is mid-sulk: I like you more than I'm good at showing. I'd like this to be the real thing. Are you in? Choose your words like they cost money. With Sin, they kind of do.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Steel and silver. Same metal, different polish.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong, true and harsh is still harsh. Sin, cold and perfect is still cold.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Say it plainly. Then let one blunt line slide.

im-water.title: Excellent teammates, lonely lovers
im-water.text: An Im Water is the deep current to your cold steel. You both have clear minds and strong opinions, and together you can solve almost anything. You've probably moved a sofa together without a single argument. You've definitely debated something at 1 a.m. and enjoyed it. The drift in this situationship is that you become excellent teammates and lonely lovers. Plenty of action, not enough tenderness. You want commitment and clear plans; Im wants freedom and flexibility. You ask 'are we doing Saturday?' and Im says 'let's see'. You find that maddening. Im finds your bluntness a bit chilly. Both of you are independent, so neither of you rushes toward the soft conversation. The 'what are we' question becomes one more logistic that never quite gets scheduled. Im's bursts and silences frustrate you, and your directness can make Im go further out. Your signal is clarity, which an ocean can feel as a fence. For the talk, ask for commitment and offer freedom in the same breath: I want us to be together. I don't need to know your every move. I do need to know we're a couple. Then agree on a minimum check-in and respect the rest.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Cold steel, deep water. Clear minds, strong currents.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Excellent teammates. Now try being lovers on purpose.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Commitment and freedom in the same sentence. You can.

gye-water.title: The fog photo with no caption
gye-water.text: A Gye Water is the morning dew on your sword. Soft, quiet, and somehow the only thing that makes you go gentle. Gye sends you a photo of fog with no caption, and you find yourself staring at it longer than you'd admit. You want to protect them. That instinct is lovely and also where things wobble. The drift in this situationship is speed. You want answers now. Gye needs a day to know what they feel. When you ask 'so are we together or not', Gye can go misty, and you get louder. Then Gye vanishes for a bit, and you get louder still, and suddenly the situationship is a standoff between someone who needs a straight answer and someone who doesn't have one yet. Your bluntness can hurt Gye more than you realize, and your protectiveness can tip into control. Your signal is strength, which can feel like pressure to someone this quiet. For the talk, ask your question and then give Gye time: I want to be with you. Think about it. Tell me when you know. Then wait without chasing. And when Gye sends the fog photo, ask what it means.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: The sword and the morning dew. Tough love, soft center.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong, ask what the fog photo means. It means something.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye can ask for a day, then come back with the answer.
